Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute shortness of breath at rest while watching TV; began about 1 hour prior to consult.
  - Postpartum, 4 weeks after cesarean section.
  - New cough started yesterday; nonproductive.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - SOB onset within the last hour; patient uncertain if worsening.
  - Palpitations (“heart really going”); anxiety/stress reported.
  - No chest pain with SOB; chest soreness with deep inspiration (also notes C-section area is tender).
- ENT symptoms (as applicable):
  - Not discussed in this consult.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
  - No recent illnesses beyond common colds “a few months ago.”
  - No prior hospital care or injection therapy for similar symptoms documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergy: Ibuprofen (reaction not described; not documented).
  - Medications: Codeine used regularly post-op; not taken for ~1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context:
  - At home with newborn; partner at work. Patient plans to self-transport to hospital with baby.
  - Family history: Mother had leg clots.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - Not recorded.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Patient reports shortness of breath; cough present since yesterday (dry). No stridor/noisy breathing documented.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Anxiety/stress reported. No dizziness or syncope documented.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Not recorded.
  - Patient self-counted pulse: 30 beats during clinician-timed interval; clinician noted “slightly fast heart rate.”
- Presence of another person with the patient:
  - Infant present; no other adult present.

Assessment:
- Acute shortness of breath 4 weeks post–cesarean section; high concern for postpartum thromboembolic event (e.g., pulmonary embolism).
- Justification: Sudden onset dyspnea at rest; recent C-section (4 weeks postpartum); palpitations with clinician-perceived tachycardia; nonproductive cough; family history of clots (mother).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Strongly advised immediate hospital/ED evaluation.
  - Option to call an ambulance offered; patient elected to self-transport promptly with infant.
  - Advised to avoid taking codeine for now.
- Specific instructions provided:
  - Take necessary items for the baby; proceed to hospital “fairly quickly.”
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Not documented in the transcript.
- Follow-up:
  - Not discussed. No ENT or allergy referrals discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Detailed allergy list and description of ibuprofen reaction.
  - Systematic ENT airway symptom review (throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, facial/oral/uvular swelling, stridor).
  - Full vital signs (RR, SpO2, BP, temperature), physical exam findings.
  - Smoking status, immobilization, postpartum anticoagulation history, prior VTE history, calf pain/swelling.
  - Rescue medications/devices (e.g., inhalers) not reviewed.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Date of birth conflict noted: patient stated 1980; clinician later stated 1983.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; some incomplete/unclear fragments. No in-person exam due to telehealth format.
